inspection_summary: Inspected all 680 normalized lines. The article builds totient-weighted discrete measures on the positive multiplicative reals, converts their convergence problem into Mellin-space zeta quotients, and relates admissible contour shifts to RH and more general zero-free half-planes. Reusable depth lies in the smoothness/transform-decay interface, the pole-versus-rate dictionary, the contrast with nonsmooth interval tests, and the special non-Paley-Wiener probe. Several displayed formulas are missing or garbled in extraction; units touching them retain only prose-supported claims and flag formula-level scan dependence.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction: additive comparison
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates measure convergence by Poisson summation for uniformly clustering additive atoms and smooth test functions.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction: multiplicative measures and main results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces the totient-weighted multiplicative measure family, states convergence/RH and zero-free-region criteria, records rough-test obstructions and a special probe, and locates the geometric antecedent.

sections_inspected.label: Preliminaries: Mertens and Abel summation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives baseline weak convergence first for intervals and then smooth compactly supported tests, with a horocycle-measure interpretation.

sections_inspected.label: Mellin transform and meromorphic structure
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the Mellin transform, proves its initial domain, factorizes it into test-function and zeta data, identifies possible poles, states a functional equation, and establishes vertical-strip decay.

sections_inspected.label: Zeta growth estimates
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Collects unconditional, Lindelof-equivalent, RH-conditional, and zero-free-half-plane estimates used to justify contour motion.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of Theorem A
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses Mellin inversion, residue extraction, and Riemann-Lebesgue decay to recover the baseline asymptotic.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of Theorem B: smooth-test rate criteria
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves the RH implication and converse and the general correspondence between zero-free abscissae and convergence rates.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of Theorem B: rough and special probes
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves the interval-test exponent obstruction and analyzes a special function whose transform exposes zeta zeros despite weaker decay.

sections_inspected.label: Final remark and corollary
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Specializes to an integer sequence and states a finite-sum corollary, but the decisive displays are extraction-defective.

accepted_units.title: Poisson summation turns smoothness into rapid additive-measure convergence
accepted_units.why_material: The additive lattice example isolates a reusable mechanism: uniform atom clustering plus rapid Fourier decay makes evaluation against smooth compactly supported tests approximate integration with errors smaller than any prescribed power.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a comparison family, not the totient-weighted multiplicative family used in the main theorems.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The defining display is absent from the text layer, but the Poisson-summation mechanism and conclusion are recoverable from lines 25-40; scan verification is required for the exact normalization.

accepted_units.title: Totient-weighted discrete measures on the positive multiplicative group
accepted_units.why_material: The paper replaces the uniform additive lattice by a measure on positive reals whose discrete masses are weighted by Euler's totient function, creating the arithmetic irregularity later detected by Mellin transform and zeta factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The measure acts on compactly supported smooth functions and is treated at several differentiability levels.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The central defining display at lines 44-46 is missing; only the prose-supported construction skeleton is accepted, and exact atom locations, scaling, and normalization require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Convergence-rate dictionary for RH and zero-free half-planes
accepted_units.why_material: The main theorem makes improvement of the measure-convergence rate for every smooth test function equivalent to RH and, more generally, pairs an O(y^(a-epsilon)) rate with absence of zeta zeros in Re(s)>2(1-a).
accepted_units.context_note: The universal quantifier over test functions is essential because later the test-function Mellin factor can be chosen not to vanish at a proposed zeta zero.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several exponents and the Theorem A display are typographically damaged; the general zero-free mapping in lines 79-83 is readable, while exact formula reuse requires the scan.

accepted_units.title: Characteristic functions impose a sharp rough-test exponent barrier
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem separates smooth-test contour behavior from nonsmooth tests by asserting that interval characteristics cannot enjoy arbitrarily improved convergence and that the stated exponent is best possible for some nonsmooth functions.
accepted_units.context_note: The later lemma at lines 467-502 supplies the arithmetic contradiction behind this obstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The limiting display is partially garbled; the prose identifies the optimal-exponent conclusion, but scan verification is required for its exact numerical rendering.

accepted_units.title: A designated test function detects zeros approaching Re(s)=1
accepted_units.why_material: A single specially chosen function is asserted to convert extreme failure of the convergence rate into the statement that zeta zeros occur arbitrarily close to the line Re(s)=1, providing a targeted alternative to the all-test-function criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof later exploits this function's unusually transparent Mellin-transform poles and sufficient, though non-Paley-Wiener, decay.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definition of the function and one displayed limit are missing or damaged; the stated iff meaning is readable, but the exact probe must be recovered from the scan before reuse.

accepted_units.title: The discrete-measure problem descends from a horocycle-measure formulation
accepted_units.why_material: The author explicitly connects the construction to Zagier's relation between RH and horocyclic measures on the modular orbifold, locating the arithmetic measure model as a continuation of a geometric-dynamical viewpoint.
accepted_units.context_note: This span gives provenance and a bridge, not an argument establishing the cited geometric equivalence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-only and stable in the normalized text.

accepted_units.title: Mertens plus Abel summation lifts interval asymptotics to smooth tests
accepted_units.why_material: The paper first evaluates interval tests using the summatory behavior of the totient function and then uses Abel summation and uniform approximation to extend the baseline convergence estimate to compactly supported smooth or continuous functions.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an elementary route to Theorem A, later rederived by Mellin inversion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Intermediate displays are degraded, but the named inputs and extension argument are explicit in lines 139-162; exact constants and powers require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Mertens convergence becomes equidistribution of periodic horocycles
accepted_units.why_material: The source interprets the same limiting statement geometrically: periodic-orbit horocycle measures, normalized by arc length, converge vaguely to Haar measure as their periods grow.
accepted_units.context_note: The overlap with the analytic derivation is intentional because these lines reframe rather than merely continue it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose statement is clear; the group/quotient typography is mildly damaged but not needed for the semantic bridge.

accepted_units.title: Mellin transform packages the entire measure family as a distribution-valued analytic object
accepted_units.why_material: Integrating m_y(f) against y^(s-2) gives a holomorphic transform on its initial half-plane and, when test functions vary, a weakly holomorphic measure- or distribution-valued function intended for meromorphic continuation.
accepted_units.context_note: Compact support also makes m_y(f) vanish for sufficiently large y, so the analytic issue is concentrated near y=0.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transform definition and convergence half-plane are readable despite symbol substitutions; exact notation should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Logarithmic transport exposes irregular weighted support and a Farey-sequence connection
accepted_units.why_material: Pulling the multiplicative measures back along the exponential map turns them into discrete measures on the real line whose irregular support and totient weights explain why their errors differ from the uniformly spaced Poisson example and connect them to Farey-sequence criteria.
accepted_units.context_note: This span diagnoses the structural source of arithmetic difficulty rather than proving a rate theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-only mechanism is recoverable; exact notation for the pushed measure is OCR-degraded.

accepted_units.title: The Mellin transform separates the test function from a zeta quotient
accepted_units.why_material: Changing variables term by term factorizes the transform into an entire Mellin factor determined by f and a quotient of zeta functions. Meromorphic continuation then turns zeta zeros into possible poles, except where the chosen test factor cancels them.
accepted_units.context_note: The simple pole at s=1 produces the limiting measure; other possible poles include negative integers and zeros of zeta(2s) in the stated strip.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Key displayed quotients are visually degraded but the factorization, entire test factor, continuation, residue role, and pole locations are stated in prose; formula-level use requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Smooth compact support yields rapid vertical-strip Mellin decay
accepted_units.why_material: Repeated integration by parts places the test-function Mellin factor in a Paley-Wiener class, giving rapid decay uniformly on fixed vertical strips and the L1 integrability needed for Mellin inversion and contour shifts.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the technical interface by which test-function regularity controls accessible convergence rates.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several bounds are absent, but the rapid-decay and L1 conclusions are explicit in lines 307-324.

accepted_units.title: Zeta growth and reciprocal bounds govern admissible contour motion
accepted_units.why_material: The source records growth exponents for zeta, a Lindelof-equivalent critical-line estimate, and Littlewood bounds under RH or a general zero-free half-plane. These estimates control the zeta quotient on vertical lines after the test factor has supplied rapid decay.
accepted_units.context_note: These are recalled classical inputs rather than results proved in the article; their role is operational in the later contour arguments.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Many displayed inequalities are partially lost, but their hypotheses, qualitative bounds, and cited roles are recoverable from the surrounding prose; exact estimates require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Residue extraction plus Riemann-Lebesgue decay proves baseline convergence
accepted_units.why_material: Mellin inversion expresses m_y(f) on a vertical line; moving the contour crosses the pole at s=1, whose residue is the limiting functional, while the remaining vertical integral decays by Riemann-Lebesgue.
accepted_units.context_note: This gives the transform-theoretic proof of Theorem A and exhibits the reusable pole-to-main-term pattern.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The residue and remainder displays are damaged, but the contour, pole, integrability, and decay logic are stated explicitly.

accepted_units.title: RH is equivalent to a universal smooth-test contour shift
accepted_units.why_material: Under RH the zeta bounds permit shifting the Mellin inversion line and yield the advertised error rate. Conversely, a universal rate analytically continues every M_f into the corresponding half-plane; choosing f whose entire Mellin factor does not vanish at a candidate zero prevents cancellation and forces the zeta quotient to be holomorphic there.
accepted_units.context_note: The converse depends on universality over f, not merely a favorable individual test.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The contour displays are partly degraded, but the two directions and the noncancellation choice are clear in lines 423-455.

accepted_units.title: The rightmost zeta zero sets the attainable convergence exponent
accepted_units.why_material: Writing beta for the supremum of real parts of zeta zeros, the source derives a convergence rate from vertical-line integrability and reverses the implication: a rate with exponent a rules out zeros in Re(s)>2(1-a).
accepted_units.context_note: This generalizes the RH boundary case into a continuous rate-versus-zero-free-region correspondence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One interval endpoint is OCR-corrupted, but the beta definition, forward rate, and converse half-plane are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Prime-step jumps obstruct overfast convergence for interval tests
accepted_units.why_material: The proof rewrites interval-test error through the summatory totient function and shows that an assumed overfast remainder would force a bounded expression; evaluating its discrete recurrence at integers whose successor is prime instead makes it unbounded.
accepted_units.context_note: This isolates discontinuity and arithmetic jumps as an obstruction absent from the smooth Paley-Wiener regime.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The recurrence displays are substantially garbled, but the contradiction strategy, prime subsequence, bounded-versus-unbounded conclusion, and extension to arbitrary intervals are recoverable; exact algebra requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A non-Paley-Wiener test has poles only at zeta-zero locations
accepted_units.why_material: For the designated function F, its Mellin transform has no other poles in Re(s)>0 than those contributed by zeros of zeta(2s). Although the transform lacks rapid Paley-Wiener decay, it decays sufficiently to shift inversion to a line determined by the rightmost zeta zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The clean pole structure makes F a sharper diagnostic than a generic test whose entire factor may cancel a zero.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The formula for F and its Mellin transform is missing; the pole claim and decay comparison are explicit, so exact reuse requires scan recovery.

accepted_units.title: Residual Fourier decay makes the special probe rule out beta below one
accepted_units.why_material: Assuming the supremum beta of zero real parts is below one, the paper bounds the shifted-line integrand and its derivative, obtains a contour representation, and identifies the remainder with a Fourier transform in log y. Integration by parts and Riemann-Lebesgue force that remainder to decay, contradicting the probe's hypothesized large normalized error.
accepted_units.context_note: Together with the pole structure, this proves the special-function direction linking the extreme error behavior to zeros arbitrarily close to Re(s)=1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several integrands and exponents are degraded, but the rectangle shift, vanishing horizontal edges, Fourier/log change, decay, and contradiction are explicit; precise bounds require scan verification.
